name: Jason
overview: Jason is a male figure noted in the New Testament as the owner of the house where the apostles Paul and Silas stayed during their ministry in Thessalonica. Scripture does not specify his tribal affiliation or other personal details. His role is primarily connected to providing hospitality and support to early Christian missionaries.
namesAndTitles: The name Jason appears once in the New Testament without a given meaning or divine origin. It is presented simply as a proper name without additional significance noted in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Jason beyond his association as the host of Paul and Silas. No further familial connections are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jason's significance lies in his hospitality and support to Paul and Silas during their missionary work in Thessalonica, offering them a place of refuge. This act demonstrates the early Christian community's commitment to aiding the spread of the gospel despite opposition. His home served as a key location in the narrative of the apostles' ministry, highlighting the practical role of believers in advancing the church.
